title: Evaluation harness: metric adapter for multi-task scoring across FP8/INT8 profiles
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Problem: We need a modular, testable metric adapter layer in the eval harness that can compute and aggregate task-specific quality metrics (perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, Rouge/BLEU, token-level F1, and custom scorers) consistently across different quantization profiles (FP8, INT8). Current validation code is fragmented: separate scripts for each metric, inconsistent preprocessing/tokenization rules, and no standard handling of streaming outputs or KV-cache truncated sequences. This leads to brittleness when comparing baseline float models to quantized variants and makes rollout/quality gates noisy.

Goal: Implement a metric adapter abstraction that: 1) normalizes predictions and references (tokenization, whitespace, case, detokenization rules) per model family and task; 2) exposes a uniform API for unit tests and the eval pipeline; 3) supports streaming/partial outputs and post-hoc aggregation; 4) computes per-slice and aggregated confidence intervals using bootstrap sampling; 5) integrates task weighting and calibration-aware penalties so that quant profile regressions that matter for customer workloads are surfaced.

Success criteria:
- Single 'metrics adapter' package used by the calibration pipeline, quant validation jobs, and CI-based quality gates.
- Reproducible metric outputs with deterministic seeds and documented randomization behavior.
- Coverage for: perplexity (masked & denoising contexts), MMLU-style multi-choice accuracy and calibrated score aggregation, sequence-level Rouge/BLEU for summarization/translation, token-level F1 and span scoring for NER/extractive QA, and plug-in hooks for customer task scorers.
- Aggregated composite score (task-weighted) and per-task deltas between float and quant profiles with 95% bootstrap CIs.
- Unit tests and end-to-end validation on a small reference suite; dashboard panels in Console showing per-profile delta and failure slices.

Design notes / approach:
- Adapter interface: register(metric_name, config) -> returned object exposes compute(batch_predictions, batch_references, metadata) -> returns scalar(s) and optional per-example breakdown. Implement canonical adapters: perplexity_adapter, mmlu_adapter, nlg_adapter (rouge/bleu), token_f1_adapter, span_f1_adapter. Each adapter will accept a normalizer object to handle tokenization/detokenization idiosyncrasies of different model families.
- Normalization: central library with model-family rules (gpt-style, llama-style, t5-style) for whitespace, punctuation, hyphenation, and numeric formatting. Normalizer must be configurable per-run; default rules documented in Confluence.
- Streaming / partial outputs: adapters must support incremental scoring by accepting ordered partial tokens and a flag when a response is final. For metrics that require final sequence (Rouge/BLEU), buffer partials and score once final flag seen. For perplexity and token-level metrics, allow scoring on the fly with careful handling of context windows and KV-cache trimming.
- Calibration-aware weighting: a post-processor will downweight low-confidence tokens or responses according to calibrated model confidence (logit transforms / temperature scaling). This helps emphasize user-facing regressions for rare but high-impact classes.
- Statistical methods: default to 1000 bootstrap resamples for CI; configurable. Provide t-test and bootstrap p-values for pairwise comparisons float vs quant. For multi-task aggregation, compute weighted mean and use bootstrap across tasks respecting task sample sizes.
- Deterministic seeding: all sampling must accept a seed string derived from job id + profile id to ensure reproducible runs in CI and nightly validation.
- Performance: implement streaming-friendly metric computation with sharded accumulators to handle large eval sets without full materialization. Memory-safe design to run on dedicated workers used by nightly quant sweep.

Planned tasks / milestones:
- T1 (this ticket): implement adapter interfaces, normalizer rules for three model families, perplexity_adapter, and mmlu_adapter prototypes. Add unit tests and small conftest fixtures.
- T2: implement nlg_adapter (Rouge/BLEU) using sacrebleu/rouge wrappers and ensure deterministic tokenizer choices.
- T3: token/span scorers for NER/QA and calibration-aware post-processor.
- T4: bootstrap CI module and CLI for running pairwise float vs quant comparisons and generating per-slice reports.
- T5: integrate outputs to Console Metrics dashboard (panel spec + ingestion shim).

Risks / tradeoffs:
- Sacrebleu and ROUGE libraries have minor version incompatibilities; we will vendor a deterministic wrapper to avoid drift.
- Perplexity comparisons across task types require consistent batching and masking; we will document constraints and surface warnings in the adapter when invalid configurations are detected.
- Calibration weighting could mask true regressions if misconfigured; default behavior is to present both raw and calibrated scores.

QA / validation plan:
- Unit tests for each adapter covering edge cases (empty outputs, truncated sequences, streaming partials).
- End-to-end test on a 500-example reference suite that includes multi-choice, summarization, translation, and extractive QA. Compare float baseline to INT8/FP8 profiles and verify delta reporting and CI computation.
- Canary job: add a nightly quant-compare job that writes results to S3 and triggers dashboard ingestion.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main with feature flag 'metric-adapter-v2' off.
- Run internal validation in staging quant job for 1 week.
- Flip feature flag and update CI quality gates to require composite score thresholds for dedicated/hosted rollouts.

updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed. Prototype mmlu_adapter using existing multi-choice harness. Observed mismatch in tokenization for our T5-family models; added normalizer rule set entry 't5-numeric-normalize'.

2025-02-18: Design review with Product and Applied ML. Agreed to include calibration-aware weighting but keep raw/unweighted outputs by default. Lina to own adapter API shape. Action: schedule sacrebleu vendor decision.

2025-02-24: Implementation: base adapter and perplexity_adapter landed in feature branch. Unit tests added for streaming partials. CI failing due to rouge package version; pinned rouge_score==0.1.3 in test env.

2025-03-01: Integration with bootstrap CI module started. First end-to-end run (float vs int8) completed on small suite. Preliminary results show mean composite delta: -0.8% (95% CI [-1.5%, -0.1%]) for int8 on the suite. Saved artifacts to S3 (s3://redwood-quant-eval/ENG-15230/run-20250301/).
notes: Avoid duplicating tokenizer logic in adapters; import central Normalizer. Coordinate with Console team for panel schema. Follow release checklist for runtime-1.22.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All canonical adapters implemented and unit tested. 2) E2E run comparing float vs INT8/FP8 produces reproducible deltas and bootstrap CIs. 3) CI quality gate can ingest composite score and flag regressions. 4) Docs and Confluence updated.
